uiStrings_appDescription: Discover your network's NAT type and learn how it affects gaming, P2P applications, and connectivity.
uiStrings_privacyNote: All detection happens in your browser using public STUN servers. Nothing is sent to our servers.
uiStrings_analyzingNetwork: Analyzing your network configuration using STUN servers...
uiStrings_detectionTimeInfo: This usually takes 3–10 seconds. Maximum wait time: 15 seconds.
uiStrings_readyToDetect: Ready to detect your NAT type
uiStrings_footerInfo: This tool measures NAT mapping behavior with WebRTC and public STUN servers. Browsers cannot observe filtering behavior, so cone subtypes (Full, Restricted, Port-Restricted) are never claimed.
uiStrings_natTypeIdentified: Your NAT type has been successfully identified
uiStrings_otherNATTypesDescription: Learn about different NAT types and how they affect connectivity.
uiStrings_natTypeInconclusive: Not enough STUN servers responded to determine your NAT type
uiStrings_confidenceReasons_mULTIPLE_SER: Several STUN servers on different networks all observed the same external address from the same local socket.
STUN servers on different networks observed different external ports from the same local socket.
uiStrings_confidenceReasons_sINGLE_SERVE: Only one STUN server responded, so mapping behavior across destinations could not be compared.
uiStrings_confidenceReasons_nO_MAPPINGS: No STUN server responded, but your local address is public, suggesting a direct connection.
uiStrings_natTypesNote_intro: Classic NAT names mix two independent properties.
uiStrings_natTypesNote_mappingDescriptio: Does the same local socket get the same external port for every destination? This separates Cone NAT from Symmetric NAT.
uiStrings_natTypesNote_filteringDescript: Who may send packets back through a mapping? This splits Cone NAT into Full, Restricted, and Port-Restricted.

natTypes_CONE_NAT_definition: Endpoint-independent mapping: the same local socket keeps the same external IP:port for every destination. This is what the tool reports; Full, Restricted, and Port-Restricted Cone are its filtering subtypes.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_exampleScenario_0: Gaming: Most multiplayer games work well. Hosting servers is possible with UPnP or port forwarding.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_exampleScenario_1: P2P File Sharing: BitTorrent and similar applications achieve good speeds with direct peer connections.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_exampleScenario_2: Video Calls: WebRTC applications (Zoom, Teams, Meet) establish peer-to-peer connections successfully.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_exampleScenario_3: Remote Access: VPN clients and SSH connections work reliably through NAT traversal.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_troubleshootingTip_0: Enable UPnP/NAT-PMP on your router for automatic port mapping by applications.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_troubleshootingTip_1: For hosting game servers, configure static port forwarding in your router settings.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_troubleshootingTip_2: If some P2P connections fail, ensure your firewall allows bidirectional UDP traffic.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_troubleshootingTip_3: Consider using IPv6 if available to bypass NAT entirely for supported applications.
natTypes_CONE_NAT_comparison: Cone NAT provides consistent external port mapping (good for P2P), unlike Symmetric NAT which creates different mappings per destination (breaks P2P). Subtype detection requires advanced STUN servers not available in browsers.
natTypes_FULL_CONE_definition: The most permissive NAT type. Once an internal address is mapped to an external address and port, any external host can send packets to that mapping. This allows the easiest connectivity for peer-to-peer applications.
natTypes_FULL_CONE_exampleScenario_0: Gaming: You can host multiplayer game servers that friends can join directly without port forwarding.
natTypes_FULL_CONE_exampleScenario_1: P2P File Sharing: BitTorrent clients achieve maximum speeds with direct peer connections.
natTypes_FULL_CONE_exampleScenario_2: Video Calls: WebRTC applications establish peer-to-peer connections without relay servers.
natTypes_FULL_CONE_troubleshootingTip_0: This is the best NAT type for connectivity. No changes needed.
natTypes_FULL_CONE_troubleshootingTip_1: If you experience issues, verify that UPnP is enabled on your router for automatic port mapping.
natTypes_FULL_CONE_troubleshootingTip_2: Consider static port forwarding in your router settings for critical applications (gaming, dedicated servers).
natTypes_FULL_CONE_comparison: Full Cone NAT is more permissive than Restricted Cone (which filters by source IP) and far better than Symmetric NAT (which changes mappings per destination).
natTypes_RESTRICTED_CONE_definition: A moderately permissive NAT type. Once an internal address sends data to an external IP, that external IP (from any of its ports) can send data back. More restrictive than Full Cone, but still allows good P2P connectivity.
natTypes_RESTRICTED_CONE_exampleScenario: Gaming: Most multiplayer games work well. Hosting servers requires the game server to respond from the same IP you connected to.
P2P File Sharing: BitTorrent works well since peers exchange IP addresses through trackers before connecting.
Video Calls: Works well for most applications. Some corporate firewalls may cause issues.
natTypes_RESTRICTED_CONE_troubleshooting: This NAT type works well for most applications. If you experience issues, try enabling UPnP on your router.
For hosting game servers, configure static port forwarding for the specific game ports.
If connectivity fails, check whether your application requires Full Cone NAT (rare).
natTypes_RESTRICTED_CONE_comparison: Restricted Cone NAT adds IP-based filtering compared to Full Cone, but is much better than Symmetric NAT, which creates new mappings per destination.
natTypes_PORT_RESTRICTED_CONE_definition: The most common type on home routers. Return traffic is only accepted from the exact IP:port the internal host contacted first. Hole punching still works because both peers contact each other's endpoint through a signaling server.
natTypes_PORT_RESTRICTED_CONE_exampleSce: Gaming: Works for most matchmaking systems. Hosting servers may require manual port forwarding.
P2P File Sharing: BitTorrent works, but may experience reduced connectivity compared to Full Cone NAT.
Video Calls: Most modern apps (Zoom, Teams, Meet) handle this automatically using STUN/TURN servers.
natTypes_PORT_RESTRICTED_CONE_troublesho: Enable UPnP/NAT-PMP on your router to allow applications to configure port mappings automatically.
For gaming servers, configure static port forwarding with specific port ranges in your router settings.
Consider upgrading your router firmware to support Full Cone or Restricted Cone NAT if available.
natTypes_PORT_RESTRICTED_CONE_comparison: Port-Restricted Cone adds port-level filtering on top of Restricted Cone's IP filtering. More secure, but requires NAT traversal for P2P applications.
natTypes_SYMMETRIC_definition: The most restrictive NAT type. Creates a unique mapping for each destination IP and port combination. External hosts cannot predict the public port, making peer-to-peer connections very difficult without relay servers.
natTypes_SYMMETRIC_exampleScenario_0: Gaming: Cannot host servers. Matchmaking may fail or require relay servers (higher latency).
natTypes_SYMMETRIC_exampleScenario_1: P2P File Sharing: BitTorrent relies on tracker/DHT, but cannot accept incoming connections (slower speeds).
natTypes_SYMMETRIC_exampleScenario_2: Video Calls: Most apps (Zoom, Teams, WhatsApp) work via TURN relay servers, increasing latency.
natTypes_SYMMETRIC_troubleshootingTip_0: Contact your ISP: Symmetric NAT is often imposed by mobile carriers or CGNAT. Request a public IPv4 address if available.
natTypes_SYMMETRIC_troubleshootingTip_1: Use a VPN: A VPN with port forwarding can bypass Symmetric NAT restrictions for specific applications.
natTypes_SYMMETRIC_troubleshootingTip_2: IPv6: If your ISP supports IPv6, enable it to bypass NAT entirely (requires IPv6-capable applications).
natTypes_SYMMETRIC_comparison: Symmetric NAT is the opposite of Full Cone NAT. While Full Cone allows anyone to connect, Symmetric creates unique mappings per destination, preventing direct P2P connectivity.
natTypes_NO_NAT_definition: Your device has a public IP address and is directly connected to the internet without any NAT translation. This provides the best possible connectivity for all applications, but may expose your device to direct internet traffic.
natTypes_NO_NAT_exampleScenario_0: Gaming: Perfect for hosting game servers. No port forwarding or NAT configuration needed.
natTypes_NO_NAT_exampleScenario_1: P2P File Sharing: Maximum connectivity and speeds. Can seed and download simultaneously.
natTypes_NO_NAT_exampleScenario_2: Remote Access: Can run SSH, web servers, or VPN servers without port forwarding.
natTypes_NO_NAT_troubleshootingTip_0: IMPORTANT: Enable a firewall on your device or router to protect against unauthorized access.
natTypes_NO_NAT_troubleshootingTip_1: Only open ports for services you actually use. Close all unnecessary ports.
natTypes_NO_NAT_troubleshootingTip_2: Consider using a hardware firewall or router in front of your device for additional security.
natTypes_NO_NAT_comparison: No NAT provides the best connectivity, but requires manual security configuration. NAT provides automatic (though imperfect) security through obscurity.
natTypes_MULTIPLE_LAYERS_definition: You are behind two NAT devices, typically a home router behind your ISP's carrier-grade NAT (CGNAT). Each layer translates addresses independently, and you can only configure the inner one.
natTypes_MULTIPLE_LAYERS_exampleScenario: Gaming: Cannot host servers. Even client connections may fail for games requiring specific NAT types.
P2P File Sharing: Severely limited. Can only download from peers; cannot seed or upload effectively.
Remote Access: Cannot expose services (SSH, web server) without complex tunneling solutions (ngrok, Tailscale).
natTypes_MULTIPLE_LAYERS_troubleshooting: Request a public IP from your ISP: Some ISPs offer public IPv4 addresses for a fee (removes the CGNAT layer).
Use IPv6: Enable IPv6 on your router and devices to bypass NAT entirely (if your ISP supports native IPv6).
VPN or Tunneling Service: Use Tailscale, ZeroTier, or ngrok to expose services through encrypted tunnels.
natTypes_MULTIPLE_LAYERS_comparison: Compared with a single home NAT, the outer layer is outside your control: port forwarding, UPnP, and DMZ settings on your router no longer expose services, and the effective behavior is that of the most restrictive layer.
natTypes_UNKNOWN_definition: Fewer than two STUN servers responded, so the mapping behavior of your NAT could not be compared across destinations. Try again, or switch networks if outbound UDP is restricted.
uiStrings_detectableSectionDescription: Mapping behavior is measured by comparing the external address that several STUN servers report for the same local socket.
uiStrings_filteringSectionDescription: These classic names describe who may send packets back through a mapping. A browser cannot observe this, so the tool reports all of them as Cone NAT.
uiStrings_notFoundDescription: The page you are looking for does not exist or has moved.
